summary: The failure mechanism is established: settlement-service's consumption collapsed at ~07:42Z (61.6 → 0.4 req/s in the 07:40Z bucket) exactly as consumer lag began climbing monotonically, and the logs show a verbatim deserialization failure on a single record (orders-3@8841207, "missing required field qty; schema v1 expected, header says v2") followed by a poison-message hot-loop with attempt counters ~92k and an explicit "partition blocked", with CPU pinned at 60-71% consistent with busy retry rather than an idle or dead consumer. Broker/producer ingress stayed flat (~2.5k msg/s) and the downstream ledger-db path showed no distress, and four complete keyword searches positively excluded rebalance/revocation/assignment/session churn, so H3 and H4 are dead. However, the origin is not established: the one load-bearing hop of H1 — that order-service dep-6010 authored the orders-3 record — is supported only by strong naming/field correlation (qty→quantity, "venue", header v2) and by the absence of any other producer schema change in the window, because no queryable artifact in the toolset binds any producer to the orders-3 topic. Because the decisive hop is unprovable with the available data and the alternative origin (payment-service as publisher, and v2-body vs mislabeled-v1-body) remains open, the ranking cannot be defended at 0.66 confidence, and this report is honestly inconclusive.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 event schema change (qty→quantity, header v2) produced records settlement-service cannot deserialize, causing a poison-record hot-loop that blocks partition orders-3
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010, deployed 07:40Z) renamed 'qty' to 'quantity', added a 'venue' field and an event schema version header v2 on the OrderExecuted event. settlement-service's OrderExecuted deserializer, asserting schema v1, rejects the first v2-header record (orders-3@8841207) at 07:42:14Z with 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. The consumer retries the same offset endlessly (attempt counters ~92k), the partition is explicitly reported 'blocked', throughput flatlines at ~0.4 req/s, lag grows ~1k msg/10min and CPU pins at 60-71% from busy retry-looping. Broker ingress and the downstream DB path are both demonstrably healthy, and four complete untruncated keyword searches positively rule out rebalance/assignment churn, so the fault originates in the producer's schema/header change, not in the consumer's settings, the broker, or the DB. OPEN DETAIL (not a separate hypothesis): whether the payload body is a genuine v2 body the consumer must learn, or a v1-shaped body mislabeled v2 by the producer. Either way the trigger is the producer-side schema/header transition introduced by dep-6010 (the only producer schema change in the window) and the blocker is the consumer's inability to cope; the fix owner is the same.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) deployed 07:40Z renames 'qty'→'quantity', adds 'venue', emits schema version header v2 on OrderExecuted — the sole producer-side schema change and sole deployment in the window
Settlement stalls at the same time: throughput collapses in the 07:40Z bucket (61.6→0.4 req/s) and lag climbs monotonically from ~48 to ~62k

First error is a deserialization failure on OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' at 07:42:14Z — the event name, the field rename and the v1/v2 header in the error match the dep-6010 change record exactly
The same single offset is retried in a hot loop with huge attempt counters and the partition is reported blocked (poison message) — the only partition-related log activity on orders-3

Consumer-side busy retry loop rather than an idle/assignment-less process: CPU 60-71%, health ok, no restart, zero rebalance/revocation/assignment/session/group signatures in complete truncated=false searches

Broker and producers are healthy (messages_in steady ~2.5k/s), so the stall is neither a producer publish collapse nor broker saturation; the graph confirms documented, unmodified producer connections into the shared broker

DB write path and ledger-db are not distressed (pool flat ~6, p99 flat ~240ms, ledger-db cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min), and no posting-API errors are logged, so a downstream dependency is not producing the stall

assumptions: order-service is the producer of the OrderExecuted records settlement-service consumes on orders-3. No declared topic binding exists in any queryable artifact: the settlement-service upstream query is empty (F6), kafka's graph edges carry no topic/event names (F30, F36), order-service's queue-produce edge carries no topic (F31, F37), the dep-6010 change record names OrderExecuted and schema v2 but no topic (F40), and no config binds a producer to a topic (F41). The link therefore rests on tight naming/field correlation (qty→quantity, 'venue', header v2 in dep-6010 vs the consumer error) plus the absence of any other producer schema change in the window (F35). This is strong correlation, not a declared binding — the load-bearing hop of the whole case.
The v2 OrderExecuted records began landing on orders-3 at/just after the 07:40Z deploy; the exact first-publish timestamp is not directly observed, only the consumer's first rejection at 07:42:14Z.

Whether the v2 payload body is genuine-v2-shaped or v1-shaped-but-mislabeled remains open; this does not change the originating service or the trigger, only whether order-service must fix serialization or settlement-service must upgrade its deserializer.

Whether the deserialization error being unique to settlement-service (F19, F23) reflects 'only settlement-service still asserts schema v1' rather than a settlement-only defect; equally readable both ways.

ranked_hypotheses.title: The settlement-service poll-setting change (max.poll.records 500→200, cfg-3004) itself broke consumption
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The config change at 07:35Z reducing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 (cfg-3004, applied 07:35:37Z, ~6-7 min before onset) altered consumption behavior — smaller batches interacting with per-record processing time, session/heartbeat timing, or rebalance behavior — causing settlement-service to stall with growing lag independently of any bad record. The reporter's own suspicion, retained because a poll-batch change is the only config change in the window and precedes onset.

causal_chain.claim: Only config change in the window: max.poll.records 500→200 at 07:35Z by m.das, verified applied at runtime 07:35:37Z, preceding onset ~07:42Z
Consumption collapses ~07:42Z and lag climbs monotonically
Smaller poll batches would slow throughput toward zero and could interact badly with per-record processing or retry timing
The setting could have changed how the consumer handled the poisoned offset (retry timing) without leaving a rebalance/group signature

assumptions: A poll-batch reduction from 500 to 200 can drive throughput to ~0 (not merely slower) without any assignment-loss, rebalance, session-timeout or group-churn signature; no measurement supports this and the observed mechanism is explicitly a single-offset poison loop, not reduced batch throughput.

The config could be the proximate trigger of the retry behavior on offset 8841207 without being the reason that offset is unprocessable — the record is unprocessable by schema, which the config did not change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db contention from neighbour services blocked settlement writes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared postgres ledger-db, written by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service, developed contention (locks/connection saturation) that blocked settlement-service's write path, freezing per-message handling and letting lag grow.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db is shared by four services including settlement-service
settlement throughput collapses and lag climbs from ~07:42Z
DB contention/locks on the shared DB stall the consumer's write call

assumptions: A lock/wait problem could exist while CPU and slow_queries_per_min stay flat — not verified; no lock metric exists for ledger-db, so the rejection rests on flat cpu/slow_queries plus flat consumer pool/latency.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: ledger-db CPU flat ~30% and slow_queries flat ~1/min (F16), settlement-service db_pool_in_use flat ~6 with latency_p99_ms flat ~240ms (F15), and no posting/DB errors in logs (F18) across the whole window; the observed errors are deserialization failures on a specific offset, not DB errors (F9, F10). A shared-DB contention cause cannot explain a poison record on offset 8841207. Rejection is indirect (no lock metric) but consistent across four independent series.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Producer-side or broker-side failure (partition reassignment or rebalance storm) stalled the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A kafka/broker-side event (partition reassignment or rebalance storm, per HIST-112/HIST-104 precedent) caused settlement-service to lose or churn partition assignment and stop consuming, with lag accumulating.

causal_chain.claim: Historical precedent HIST-112/HIST-104: partition reassignment / rebalance storms caused the same symptom family
Broker/producer-side issue stops delivery or churns assignment, so lag grows

Zero rebalance/revocation/assignment-loss/session-timeout signatures in four independent complete (truncated=false) searches; no rebalance metric exists at all; the only partition activity is a self-inflicted poison-message block

assumptions: A broker-side rebalance could occur without any consumer-side log signature or node metric change — now contradicted by four complete keyword searches returning zero and the absence of any rebalance metric.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Broker is healthy with steady messages_in_per_s ~2.5k/s across the window (F12, F13), so producers kept publishing and brokers were not saturated or stalled. Rather than a lost assignment the consumer actively hot-loops on one offset (F10, F28). Four independent complete (truncated=false) keyword searches return zero rebalance/revocation/assignment-loss/session/group signatures (F24-F27, F29) and no rebalance metric exists (F45), so this mechanism is positively denied, not merely unobserved. HIST-112/HIST-104 (F6) are weak historical leads, not evidence about this incident.

facts.statement: Only one config change occurred across all services in the 07:30Z-09:59Z window: settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records 500 → 200 at 07:35Z by m.das; and only one deployment: order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) at 07:40Z by a.khan (changes: rename qty→quantity, add venue, event schema version header v2), status live, not rolled back.

settlement-service throughput collapsed in the 07:40Z bucket, from ~61.6 req/s at 07:30Z to a flat 0.4 req/s from 07:50Z through 09:50Z, i.e. consumption went to ~zero right at the same bucket in which lag began climbing.

Consumer lag started climbing in the 07:40Z bucket (avg 1572, max 3512) from a healthy ~48 at 07:30Z, and grew monotonically to 59267 avg / 61605 max at 09:50Z — a steady ~1k msg/10min accumulation consistent with a stalled, not merely slow, consumer.

The first error signature is a deserialization failure: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', first seen 07:42:14Z and repeating on the same offset 213 times.

From 07:44:51Z a companion poison-message signature appears: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences, attempt counters up to ~92490) — a single offset on orders-3 is hot-looped and the partition is explicitly blocked.

settlement-service is alive but CPU-bound during the stall: cpu_pct jumped from ~27.5% (07:30Z) to ~60-71% avg (max 78.28%) through 09:50Z, consistent with busy retry-looping; health check and connection-pool stats were logged as healthy. memory_pct stayed flat (mean 49.92) and restarts were 0 for every bucket.

The broker is healthy and not the bottleneck: kafka messages_in_per_s stayed flat at ~2545.93 (07:30Z) → ~2522.73 (09:50Z), min 2226.92, max 2766.88, missing_points 0, while settlement lag grew — producers kept publishing.

The downstream write path shows no distress: settlement-service db_pool_in_use flat ~5.8-6.2 (max 6.78) and latency_p99_ms flat ~215-266 ms (mean 238.99) across the window; ledger-db cpu_pct flat ~27-33% (mean 30.08) and slow_queries_per_min flat ~0.9-1.1; no posting-API warnings/errors in settlement-service logs (total_matched 0).

Four independent complete (truncated=false) keyword searches of settlement-service logs over 04:00Z-09:59Z return ZERO rebalance ('rebalanc'), revocation ('revok'), assignment ('assign') and session ('session') signatures; the only partition-related activity is the single-record blocked-partition retry loop, and no consumer-group/rebalance metric exists (rebalance_count not_found; available_metrics limited to consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts).

No artifact binds a producer to the orders-3 topic: the settlement-service graph (depth 2, both directions) contains only queue-consume→kafka and db→ledger-db with no producer node or topic name; kafka's graph has four queue edges with no topic/event names; order-service's queue-produce edge carries no topic; dep-6010 names 'OrderExecuted' and schema v2 but no topic; no config binds a producer to a topic (order-service config query count 0); and no topic-manifest/schema-registry tool exists.

payment-service is documented as a queue-produce client into the shared kafka broker but with no topic attribution (no 'orders-3' or 'OrderExecuted' association), and no payment-service deployment or config change occurred in the 06:00Z-09:59Z window.

The verbatim deserialization signature 'missing required field qty' appears in no other consumer/publisher service's logs (portfolio-service, payment-service, order-service, notification-service all total_matched 0, truncated=false over 04:00Z-09:59Z); it is known only in settlement-service.

The metric layer shows no second failure mode: settlement-service error_rate is flat ~0.1-0.32% (including a 2-minute-bucket zoom over 07:30Z-08:00Z) with no spike at the 07:35:37Z config application or the 07:42Z onset, and restarts are 0 throughout.
The new poll setting is in effect at runtime: settlement-service logged 'config change cfg-3004 applied: consumer.max.poll.records=200' at 07:35:37Z, preceding onset.

assumptions: The producer→orders-3 link (H1's load-bearing hop) rests on correlation, not on a declared binding: order-service holds a queue-produce edge into the shared kafka broker and dep-6010 names 'OrderExecuted' plus header v2, while the consumer error names OrderExecuted with a v1/v2 header mismatch — no artifact in any available tool binds order-service (or any service) to the orders-3 topic.

payment-service is an equally documented producer into the same shared broker with no topic attribution, and it is assumed not to be the publisher of the orders-3 stream only because it had no schema/header change in the window.
The v2 records began landing on orders-3 at or just after the 07:40Z deploy; the first publish is not directly observed, only the consumer's first rejection at 07:42:14Z.

Whether the offending body is a genuine v2 body (requiring a settlement-service deserializer upgrade) or a v1-shaped body mislabeled v2 (requiring a producer serialization fix) remains open; the origin service and trigger are the same either way.

H2 (the poll-setting change as trigger) is assumed out-competed rather than falsified: neither of its mechanism hops (smaller batch → ~zero throughput with no assignment churn; config as proximate trigger of retrying an unprocessable offset) is supported by any measurement.

The uniqueness of the deserialization error to settlement-service (F19/F23) is assumed to reflect that only settlement-service still asserts schema v1, rather than a settlement-only defect; the evidence reads both ways.

Absence of rebalance/session signatures is treated as positive exclusion based on four complete truncated=false keyword searches, though a rebalance-style event worded outside rebalanc/revok/assign/session/group would not be found.
The metric layer (error_rate, restarts) is assumed not to expose the poison-message failure at all, so a hypothetical second non-HTTP-5xx failure mode would be invisible on these metrics.

timeline.event: settlement-service logs the application of cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500→200, change made 07:35Z by m.das). Last healthy state: throughput ~61.6 req/s and lag ~48 in the 07:30Z bucket.
order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010) goes live: OrderExecuted event renames qty→quantity, adds venue, adds schema version header v2. Still live, never rolled back. Kafka ingress stays flat ~2.5k msg/s.
Onset bucket: settlement-service throughput falls from ~61.6 req/s to a max of 65.3 then flatlines; consumer lag begins climbing (avg 1572, max 3512).
First error: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — repeats 213 times on the same offset.
Poison-message signature begins: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences, attempts up to ~92490); CPU pins at ~60-71%, memory and restarts flat.
Incident INC-010 reported by on-call SRE: no settlements posted ~40 min, consumer lag growing.

End of window: lag 59267 avg / 61605 max; throughput still flat at 0.4 req/s; broker ingress flat ~2522.73 msg/s; db_pool_in_use ~5.91 and latency_p99 ~215-266 ms; ledger-db cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min — downstream and broker paths undistressed.

Latest data: no rebalance/revocation/assignment/session signatures in complete keyword searches; no rebalance metric exists; error_rate flat ~0.21%; restarts 0; service remains in the blocked-partition retry loop.

recommended_actions.action: Stop the self-inflicted hot-loop: pause or stop the settlement-service consumer group's consumption of orders-3 (or disable the consumer) so the ~92k-attempt retry loop consuming 60-71% CPU ceases, and confirm cpu_pct returns toward baseline ~27%.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition is explicitly blocked and the consumer is busy-retrying one unprocessable offset (F10, F28) with CPU pinned at 60-71% (F11); halting the loop is safe, reversible, and stops resource burn without touching the broker or DB (both healthy: F12/F13, F15/F16).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back or pause order-service dep-6010 (v2.16.0) — the sole deployment in the window and the only identified producer schema/header transition — with a.khan, then watch whether settlement-service resumes processing and lag stops climbing.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010 is the only producer-side schema change in the window (rename qty→quantity, add venue, header v2) and it is still live (F2, F32, F33); if the v2 stream is what settlement-service cannot deserialize, reverting the producer removes the trigger. This also empirically tests the unproven producer→orders-3 link: no recovery after revert would argue against H1.

recommended_actions.action: Recover the blocked partition after the poison record is neutralized: either skip/seek past orders-3@8841207 or deploy a settlement-service deserializer that tolerates header v2, then confirm lag stops growing and order-processed offset advances past 8841207.
recommended_actions.rationale: Only the single offset 8841207 on orders-3 is unprocessable and blocks the partition (F9, F10, F28); advancing past it is the direct path to restoring throughput, and watching the offset advance is the definitive verification.

recommended_actions.action: Obtain the decisive artifact that binds a producer to orders-3: inspect the Kafka topic manifest / schema-registry subject-to-topic mapping / producer deployment descriptor to confirm whether order-service (or payment-service) publishes OrderExecuted to orders-3, and retrieve the raw bytes of orders-3@8841207 to determine whether the body is genuine v2 or v1-shaped mislabeled v2.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the one unproven load-bearing hop of H1 and the open question of who must change their code (F30, F36, F37, F38, F39, F40, F41); the two origin sub-questions (order-service vs payment-service; consumer upgrade vs producer serialization fix) imply different fixes.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the missing surfaces: add a consumer-group/rebalance metric and per-partition/topic Kafka metrics (ordered-3-level produce/consume counters, blocked-partition state), and capture the full untruncated settlement-service log set for the window.
recommended_actions.rationale: No rebalance/consumer-group metric exists and Kafka exposes no per-topic dimension (F45, F21), and the earlier log pull was truncated (40 of 436 lines); these gaps limit both the exclusion of H4 and the ability to see a second failure mode.

recommended_actions.action: After recovery, validate H2 cheaply: revert cfg-3004 back to consumer.max.poll.records=500 in a canary and observe whether throughput/latency change; treat the poll setting as out-competed, not exonerated.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is the only other change in the window and two of its mechanism hops carry no supporting evidence; a controlled revert gives a direct measurement of whether the smaller poll batch contributes anything beyond the poison-loop effect (F1, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Establish a schema-registry / versioned-contract gate with producer-consumer compatibility checks (fail the pipeline on backward-incompatible event changes like qty→quantity and header v1→v2) and add dead-letter-queue routing plus a bounded retry cap so a single unprocessable record can never hot-loop a partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident is a poison-record loop caused by an unversioned-tolerated producer schema transition (F2, F9, F10) on a path with no DLQ or retry cap (attempts ~92k, partition blocked); contract gating and DLQ/bounded-retry prevent the same class of recurrence regardless of which origin sub-question is resolved.

recommended_actions.action: Document the declared topic bindings (topic → producing service → consuming services → schema subject) as a queryable artifact, so future incidents can resolve producer attribution instead of relying on field-name correlation.
recommended_actions.rationale: No tool in the toolset exposes a topic manifest or producer declaration (F30, F36, F37, F38, F40, F41), which is precisely why the top hypothesis could not be closed at its claimed confidence.

data_gaps: No queryable artifact binds any producer to the orders-3 topic: the settlement-service upstream graph is empty (F6), Kafka graph edges carry no topic/event names (F30, F36), order-service's queue-produce edge has no topic (F31, F37), dep-6010 names OrderExecuted but no topic (F40), and no config binds producer to topic (F41); no topic-manifest/schema-registry tool exists in the toolset. This is the specific reason the origin could not be closed and is why the result is inconclusive rather than root_cause_identified.

payment-service is a documented producer into the shared Kafka broker with no topic attribution (F35, F39) and was not examined as a possible publisher of the orders-3 OrderExecuted stream; the environment exposes only a fixed known-services list, so an unlisted consumer could not have been tested (F20).

The raw body of orders-3@8841207 was never inspected, so it is unknown whether it is a genuine v2 payload (consumer deserializer upgrade required) or a v1-shaped body mislabeled v2 (producer serialization fix required).

Kafka exposes only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s and under_replicated_partitions — no per-topic or per-partition metrics (F21) — so it cannot be determined whether the bad v2 record family appears beyond orders-3, nor whether order-service's publish rate/v2 share on orders-3 changed at 07:40Z.

Neither Kafka broker logs nor broker CPU / under_replicated_partitions were retrievable or queried (query_logs(service=broker) and query_metrics(kafka, available_metrics) returned not_found), so broker-side resource trends and any messaging-layer rebalance/session-timeout events are unverified.

No lock/wait or connection-saturation metric exists for the shared ledger-db; H3 is excluded only indirectly via flat CPU and slow_queries (F16) and flat settlement write-path pool/latency (F15), not by a direct lock metric.

The earlier settlement-service log retrieval was truncated (40 of 436 matched lines); absence of rebalance/session signatures rests on four complete keyword searches (F24-F27) and no rebalance metric exists (F45), so a rebalance-style event worded outside rebalanc/revok/assign/session/group cannot be fully excluded.

No direct consumer-group partition-assignment state (describe-group view showing current owner/member list for orders-3) is available; absence of reassignment signatures is the only proxy for continuous ownership.

The metric layer does not expose the deserialization/poison-message failure at all (error_rate flat ~0.21% as HTTP 5xx, restarts 0, F42-F47), so a hypothetical second non-5xx failure mode would be invisible on metrics.

Producer-side service-level health (order-service errors/latency) and other services' same-window logs were not directly queried; producer behaviour is confirmed only indirectly via aggregate broker ingress (F12, F13).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A declared topic manifest, schema-registry subject→topic mapping, or producer deployment descriptor showing payment-service (not order-service) publishes OrderExecuted to orders-3 would move the origin away from dep-6010 and undercut H1's load-bearing hop.

Byte-level inspection of orders-3@8841207 showing a v1-shaped body labeled v2 by the producer would reframe the fix as an order-service serialization bug rather than a settlement-service deserializer upgrade (the trigger/owner stays the v2 schema transition either way).

Rolling back dep-6010 and observing settlement-service resume consumption and lag stop climbing would positively confirm H1; no recovery after revert would argue that the v2 producer change is not the trigger.

Evidence that settlement-service historically could consume the v2 header (e.g. compatible v2 records processed elsewhere, or a settlement-service deployment that only asserts schema v1 with no downgrade path) would shift the balance between 'consumer must be upgraded' and 'producer emitted a malformed record'.

A measured demonstration that consumer.max.poll.records 200 (cfg-3004) can drive throughput to ~0 without assignment loss or rebalance, or evidence of session/heartbeat timing change coincident with the config application, would rehabilitate H2.

Any rebalance, revocation, assignment-loss or consumer-group churn signature (log or metric) not found by the four complete keyword searches or a newly available consumer-group metric would reopen H4.

A lock/wait or connection-contention measurement on the shared ledger-db, or posted-write errors appearing in settlement-service logs, would reopen H3 — though this would not explain the specific poison record on offset 8841207.

Producer side did NOT stop: kafka messages_in_per_s stayed flat across the whole window (~2545.93 msg/s at 07:30Z -> 2522.73 msg/s at 09:50Z, min 2226.92, max 2766.88, missing_points 0) while settlement lag grew, so producers kept publishing into the broker and the stall is not a producer-side publish-rate collapse.

settlement-service consumption collapsed with the onset, not before: request_rate fell in the 07:40Z bucket from 61.58 req/s (07:30Z) to 0.4 req/s from 07:50Z onward and stayed flat at ~0.40-0.41 through 09:50Z, i.e. consumption went to ~zero right at the same bucket in which lag began climbing.

The downstream DB write path shows no distress during the window: settlement-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~5.8-6.2 connections (first 6.0, last 5.91, max 6.78) and latency_p99_ms stayed flat at ~215-266 ms (mean 238.99) from 07:30Z to 09:50Z, i.e. no connection-pool saturation and no latency blow-up on the write call.

ledger-db (the shared postgres downstream target, also written by order-service/portfolio-service/payment-service) is healthy across the window and not the bottleneck: cpu_pct flat ~27-33% (mean 30.08, min 27.12, max 33.45) and slow_queries_per_min flat ~0.9-1.1 (mean 1.0, min 0.4, max 1.62), with no step change at onset.

The new poll setting IS in effect at runtime: settlement-service logged the config application at 07:35:37Z - 'config change cfg-3004 applied: consumer.max.poll.records=200' (only one poll-config log match in the window, first and last match 07:35:37Z), which precedes onset (~07:42Z).

No downstream posting-API warnings/errors were emitted by settlement-service in this window (WARN+ search for 'posting' returned total_matched 0 over data range 04:00Z-09:59Z, truncated false), so there is no log evidence of external posting endpoint failures/timeouts; however absence in this app-log search does not prove the call path was exercised.

The verbatim deserialization signature 'missing required field qty' does NOT appear in any other consumer service's logs: portfolio-service, payment-service, order-service and notification-service each returned total_matched 0 over 04:00Z-09:59Z (truncated false). It is known to occur only in settlement-service (F9, tc-005).

The environment exposes only a fixed set of services: any consumer beyond api-gateway/auth-service/order-service/portfolio-service/pricing-engine/market-data-service/payment-service/settlement-service/notification-service/exchange-gateway and the DB/cache/broker/external components cannot be queried — 'fulfillment-service' and 'audit-service' are not known services, so potential out-of-list consumers of orders-3 could not be tested.

kafka exposes only three metrics (cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions) — no per-topic or per-partition metric, so 'does the bad record family appear on partitions/topics beyond orders-3' cannot be answered via kafka metrics; it would require a per-partition/topic query surface that does not exist.

No other consumer's logs show the schema-v1/v2 mismatch fragment on its own: order-service (the producer, which could log a serialization/read-side mismatch) returned total_matched 0 for 'schema v1 expected, header says v2' over the window.

Across the four non-settlement consumer/publisher services queried (portfolio-service, payment-service, order-service, notification-service), none shows any instance of the 'missing required field qty' error, so the observed poison-record rejection is currently attributable only to settlement-service's log surface.

A complete (untruncated) keyword search of settlement-service logs over the whole window returns ZERO rebalance signatures: contains='rebalanc' -> total_matched 0, returned 0, truncated=false over data range 04:00Z-09:59Z.
A complete keyword search returns ZERO partition-revocation signatures: contains='revok' -> total_matched 0, truncated=false over 04:00Z-09:59Z.

A complete keyword search returns ZERO consumer-group / assignment-loss signatures: contains='assign' -> total_matched 0 (tc-034) and contains='group' -> total_matched 0 (tc-047); both truncated=false over 04:00Z-09:59Z.

A complete keyword search returns ZERO session/heartbeat-timeout signatures in the consumer: contains='session' -> total_matched 0, truncated=false. The only 'heartbeat' matches are the unrelated scheduled-job heartbeat (10 INFO lines, 'scheduled job heartbeat ok', 04:17:07Z-09:56:20Z), not consumer session heartbeats.

The ONLY partition-related log activity on orders-3 is the poison-message hot-loop: contains='partition' matched 196 ERROR entries (first 07:44:51Z, last 09:58:31Z), every one the pattern 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked'. So the partition is in a self-inflicted 'blocked' state caused by an unprocessable record, not by an assignment loss.

refs.quote: poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: H4 (rebalance/reassignment as the origin) is denied by the complete log set: across four independent complete keyword searches (rebalanc, revok, assign, session) not one matching line exists, while the partition activity that IS present is single-record retry-on-blocked-partition on orders-3@8841207. This does not by itself name the origin; it only removes group-membership churn as a candidate.

The kafka service's dependency graph exposes exactly two producers into kafka and two consumers, with no topic names: edges are order-service->kafka (queue-produce), payment-service->kafka (queue-produce), settlement-service->kafka (queue-consume), notification-service->kafka (queue-consume). This is the concrete producer→topic edge family that the depth-2 settlement-service upstream query (F6) failed to expose.

order-service specifically has a queue-produce edge to kafka in its own downstream graph, alongside db->ledger-db, http->pricing-engine and http->exchange-gateway; order-service is owner 'trading', not shared.

The only deployment in the 06:00Z-09:59Z window (scope 'all services') is dep-6010 on order-service, v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z by a.khan, summary 'Order events v2', changes ['OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity','add field venue','event schema version header v2'], status 'live', rolled_back_at null. The deployed artefact is explicitly an OrderExecuted producer change, matching the exact event name in the consumer error.

The report-named version dep-6010 v2.16.0 is confirmed as the sole order-service deployment in both the incident window and a wider 2026-03-01Z→2026-05-12Z query (count 1), i.e. no earlier v2 producer rollout and no rollback in that period.

The consumer's failing record is a v2-header OrderExecuted: '(schema v1 expected, header says v2)' on orders-3 offset 8841207, while the sole producer-side change in the window is order-service's 'rename field qty -> quantity' + 'event schema version header v2' — the deployed producer change and the observed bad record are the same schema/header transition.

refs.quote: "add field venue","event schema version header v2"

findings.statement: payment-service also holds a queue-produce edge into the shared kafka broker and is therefore a possible alternative publisher of the same stream; no payment-service deployment or config change occurred anywhere in the 06:00Z-09:59Z window (deployments count 1 = dep-6010; config changes count 1 = cfg-3004), so if payment-service publishes OrderExecuted it did not change its schema/header in this window.

The kafka dependency graph exposes exactly four queue edges and NO topic or event names: order-service->kafka (queue-produce), payment-service->kafka (queue-produce), settlement-service->kafka (queue-consume), notification-service->kafka (queue-consume). There is no 'orders-3' string and no 'OrderExecuted' string anywhere in the graph output, so the graph does not declare which producer feeds which topic.

order-service's own downstream graph shows a queue-produce edge to kafka but the edge carries no topic name; the output contains no 'orders-3' or 'OrderExecuted' token, so order-service is documented as A producer into kafka, not as the producer OF orders-3.

The settlement-service graph (depth 2, both directions) contains only two edges — queue-consume to kafka and db to ledger-db — with no producer node, no topic name and no upstream edge; the consumed stream is not attributed to any producer service in the graph.

payment-service is documented as a producer into the shared kafka broker via a queue-produce edge, but holds no topic-specific declaration; the graph output does not associate payment-service with 'orders-3' or 'OrderExecuted'. So payment-service is a documented kafka producer in general but NOT documented as a producer of OrderExecuted or orders-3.

The order-service deploy record dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z) names the event 'OrderExecuted' in its change list and an event schema v2 header, but names NO topic — it does not state that order-service publishes OrderExecuted to orders-3. This is the closest artifact to a producer declaration and it omits the topic binding.

refs.quote: OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity

findings.statement: No config declaration binds a producer to a topic: the only config change in the window is settlement-service cfg-3004 on the key 'consumer.max.poll.records' (500->200); an order-service config query over 2026-03-01Z-2026-05-12T09:59Z returned count 0. Neither side carries any topic-produced-by declaration.

settlement-service error_rate (unit '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)') shows NO spike at the 07:35:37Z config application or the 07:42Z onset: it is flat and low for the entire 07:30Z-09:59Z window (mean 0.21%, min 0.1, max 0.32, missing_points 0). Values around onset are unremarkable: 07:38Z avg 0.21, 07:42Z avg 0.17, 07:46Z avg 0.17, 07:50Z avg 0.15. There is no error-rate step change of any kind, so error_rate provides no second-failure-mode signal and no evidence tying the onset (~07:42Z) or the config change (07:35:37Z) to an HTTP-5xx error burst.

A finer 2-minute-bucket zoom on error_rate across the critical 07:30Z-08:00Z stretch (bucket_seconds 120) confirms no spike at the cfg-3004 application (07:35:37Z) or at onset: 07:34Z avg 0.14, 07:36Z avg 0.18, 07:38Z avg 0.20, 07:40Z avg 0.22, 07:42Z avg 0.12, 07:44Z avg 0.22. The coarser 240s bucket does not hide any narrow error-rate burst.

settlement-service restarts = 0 for every bucket across the whole 07:30Z-09:59Z window (min 0.0, max 0.0, mean 0.0, missing_points 0, unit 'count (cumulative)'). There is NO restart at the 07:35:37Z config application, at the 07:42Z onset, or at any point during the stall, so restart/process-recycle is excluded as a failure mechanism in this window.

No consumer-group / rebalance metric exists for settlement-service: the query for 'rebalance_count' returned not_found, and the full available_metrics list is exactly [consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts] -- there is no rebalance/consumer-group/assignment metric to query. This is consistent with the earlier log-side finding (F24-F27: zero rebalanc/revok/assign/session signatures).

settlement-service memory_pct is flat across the window (mean 49.92, min 44.33, max 57.8, missing_points 0) with no rise at onset: 07:30Z avg 49.24, 07:40Z avg 50.58, 07:50Z avg 49.18, 08:00Z avg 49.59 through 09:50Z avg 49.31. Unlike cpu_pct (F11, jumped to ~60-71%), memory gives no sign of resource exhaustion or a leak and no step at 07:35:37Z or 07:42Z.

Across the two independent metric-side surfaces requested (error_rate and restarts), plus memory_pct and the full available_metrics list, there is NO error or restart signal that is NOT the known OrderExecuted deserialization/poison-message signature -- in fact the metric layer shows neither that signature nor any other: error_rate is FLAT at ~0.21% and restarts is FLAT at 0 throughout. Therefore this metric-side test neither reveals a second failure mode nor indicates a restart/error spike coinciding with the 07:42Z onset or the 07:35:37Z cfg-3004 application.
